subject: toucan
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module for a toucan model using three.js and the agentic-3js-builder SDK, following the standard build/meta export conventions and aiming for realistic scale—roughly 60 cm total length including the distinctive oversized bill.

The toucan should stand upright on the ground with feet touching y=0, keeping the model self-contained rather than relying on a separate branch prop. I'm working out the stylized anatomy: a tilted-forward body posture, black plumage with a white/cream throat and yellow-orange chest like a keel-billed toucan, plus the signature multicolored bill in green, orange, red, and yellow with a black tip, and orange periorbital skin around the eyes.

Settling on a Toco-inspired color scheme instead: black body, white throat and chest, a huge orange bill with a black tip, a blue eye patch, red undertail coverts, and dark grey-blue feet.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton and coordinate system for the toucan model — Y-up, facing +Z, roughly 0.5-0.6m tall, with a root hip joint feeding into a spine chain through the chest and neck to the head, separate chains for the tail, legs, and folded wings, and the body built as a sweep/loft along the spine with the bill, eyes, and feet added as separate shaped elements.

I'll separate the tail into its own backward-pointing chain, then set up the head and bill: a "head" joint with a child "jaw" joint for the lower mandible so the mouth can open, with upper bill geometry fixed to the head and lower bill geometry fixed to the jaw. For legs, I'm planning hip joints on each side using a limb-based approach with target and bend parameters.

Working out leg geometry with hip, knee, ankle, and toe segments to approximate a toucan's zygodactyl foot resting on the floor.

So the target is the toe tip, with the last segment running from heel to toe along the sole direction, and the chain points are hip, knee, heel, toe-end. Giving four names like ["hipL","kneeL","ankleL","footL"] produces three span joints plus a tip joint at the end, matching the leg chain's role with the foot as the tip.

For toes, rather than building full digit chains, I'll keep things simple by attaching capsule/rod toes directly to the foot joint — front toes splayed forward-left/right plus one or two back toes for a zygodactyl toucan foot.

I'm leaning toward using the existing limb IK rather than computing points manually, even though the exact bend behavior is uncertain, since it's built for this. I'm working out the geometry: target at floor height with some toe radius offset, segment lengths for thigh/shank/foot, with the heel positioned behind the toe along Z and the ankle sitting near floor level before the shank rises to the knee.

I'm realizing a flat heel-on-ground setup looks plantigrade rather than birdlike — real birds keep the ankle raised with an angled metatarsus leading down to the toes on the ground, so I probably need a three-segment limb (hip→knee→ankle→toe) where that last segment angles down rather than lying flat, solving IK to a floor-level toe target.

I'm leaning toward skipping the automatic limb helper and instead building the leg manually with explicit joint points for more control over the hip-knee-ankle-toe shape.

For toes I'll go with two forward and two back, splayed at different angles, with the foot joint as the chain tip they attach to. I'm setting up the hip-knee-ankle-foot naming convention for mirrored left/right leg chains parented off the hips joint, then moving on to designing the toucan's wings.

For the folded wing, I'm planning a flat extruded silhouette lying against the flank, working out the shoulder-elbow-wrist points and the coordinate frame so the thickness direction runs correctly along the body's side axis.

I think a single joint for the wing (role "wing") rigidly driving the extrude is simplest, rather than a full chain, since the wing is folded and doesn't need multiple articulation points.

For the tail, I'll plan it as a chain running backward from the rump, matching the toucan's medium squared tail shape with black coloring and red undertail coverts.

Now I'm thinking through the body as a swept ellipse profile along the spine chain, sizing its width and depth to match a toucan's rounded torso.

For coloring, I want to capture the classic toco toucan look: black plumage overall with a contrasting white throat and chest region, so I need to plan paint sectors to carve that out along the body sweep.

Though hard edges might look jaggy, I decide paint is simpler for defining the bib with a conditional based on normal direction and vertical position, baked as a texture in model space. Now I'm turning to the bill — a long, slightly curved, tall stylized toucan beak with serrated edge details.

I'm picturing a toco-style bill: orange body with a black tip, built as a sweep along a curved path with ellipse cross-sections tapering from a wide base near the head down to a narrow tip. Now I'm working out the base position and curve path in relation to the head joint's world coordinates.

I'm coloring the bill with a sweep that transitions from orange to black near the tip, and considering adding a subtle golden ridge along the top of the bill for a keel-billed toucan look.

Now I'm sketching the lower mandible as a jaw joint off the head, then realizing my overall body proportions are too large compared to a real toucan — I need to scale down the body, tail, and bill lengths to match a realistic ~50-60cm total length.

Let me reconsider body proportions so legs stay visible—setting hips around 0.27 with belly near 0.19 gives a usable leg length of roughly 0.19. Now I'm laying out the spine chain from rump through mid-back, chest, and neck base up to the head, thinking about how to name these joints with hips as the root of the rig.

With 5 points giving 4 spans, the neck joint sits at P3 aiming toward P4, with a separate head joint parented to it at P4, so the body sweep naturally tapers into a thin neck before the head shape. I'm now working out the radius profile along the spine's t parameter, shrinking from a rounded rump to a tapered neck near the top.

Still writing radius interpolation...

For the orientation, I'm reasoning that since the body's tangent curves from back-low to forward-up, the transported normal stays roughly vertical, making rx the sideways width and ry the height of the cross-section. I'm also planning the coloring: black body, white bib, and possibly a yellow-orange accent.

Now I'm figuring out the plumage details—thinking about whether to add subtle feather texture via a mottled black paint (mixing near-black shades) layered under the white bib pattern, nesting paint functions so the bib condition overrides the mottled base color.

I'm working out the spatial condition for the white bib/throat area using normal and position coordinates to mark the forward-facing neck region, then considering how it connects to the head, since the head itself needs both black and white zones to match the toucan's facial coloring.

For the head shape, I'm setting up a slightly stretched low-poly sphere with faceted shading for a geometric, charm-like look, and defining a paint function that uses the normal vector to split black versus white regions on the underside and front.

Now I'm thinking through how to add the bare blue skin ring around the eye socket.

Since the eye drawing is symmetric, mirroring isn't actually needed for the two sides. I'm designing the eye texture as an SVG with a blue periorbital ring, a golden-orange iris, a black pupil, and a small white highlight circle, sized for a small decal around 0.05 meters.

For positioning, I'm placing the decal relative to the head joint using local coordinates, offsetting sideways and forward on the head sphere's surface to get the eye roughly where it should sit, accounting for the sphere's radius.

The head joint itself inherits orientation from its parent neck if I don't specify an aim, which should give it a natural forward-up tilt. For the bill and other geometry built with literal points, I need to remember that unbound inputs attach to whichever joint's bone passes closest to them, so I should double check that the head's bill geometry actually binds to the head joint rather than drifting to the neck.

I'm now working out the bill's actual coordinates in model space: setting the base near the front of the head, curving the upper bill tip forward and slightly downward using a bezier with a few control points, and positioning the lower mandible hinge just behind that base so the jaw can open naturally.

I'm also sizing the bill's cross-section so it tapers from a tall, wide base down to a narrower tip, checking that the base sits plausibly against the head sphere's surface.

For colors, I'm picking a warm orange-yellow for the bill with a black tip and golden ridge accent, dark grey legs and toes with black claws, black wings, and a black tail with red-orange undertail coverts defined by angular sectors.

Working out the tail chain next: a parent joint at the hips, a broad flattened box cross-section that tapers slightly toward the tip, and a bezier path curving downward and backward from the rump to give it a natural droop.

I'll set caps to round at the start and flat at the end for the tail tip. For the wings, I'm considering whether to use a chain or a single joint parented to the chest, keeping the wing folded along the flank from shoulder to wrist with a simple outline defined in the z-y plane.

Working out the wing outline coordinates now, placing the shoulder anchor and sketching a short rounded shape sweeping backward and down to a sharp-ish tip, sized to sit against the body's flank width at that point.

Still defining wing outline...

Now thinking through leg placement: hip joints inside the body, then down to knee, ankle, and foot, trying to get a realistic bent-leg stance where the tarsus angles forward from a rear-set heel to the toes on the ground.

I'm now working out the sweep radius taper for the leg bones, thinning from thigh to foot across the joint chain.

For the toes, I'm defining four per foot: two front toes splaying outward from the foot tip at shallow angles along the floor plane, and a back toe (hallux) rooted near the ankle extending backward.

I need to make sure the capsule toes explicitly bind to the foot joint rather than auto-detecting, falling back to the last joint if tip is null. For claws, I'll add small black spike cones at each toe end using the same bone binding, and then move on to building the head as a sphere attached to the head joint's position.

For the head shape I'm scaling the sphere slightly to make it less perfectly round, matching a toucan's rounded skull, and I'm working out the paint function to color the throat and underside white versus black based on the surface normal and position within the sphere's local space.

Now I'm positioning the eye decal relative to the head joint, computing local coordinates so the eye lands on the front-side surface of the head sphere, then setting its facing direction outward from that point to orient the decal correctly.

For the eye texture itself, I'm sketching out an SVG design with concentric circles: a blue outer eye-skin disk, an iris, a dark pupil, and a small white highlight for shine, debating whether the iris should read as amber-gold or dark brown for a more toucan-like look.

I'll render that SVG into a 128px texture and apply it as a slightly raised decal onto the head surface, letting the transparent corners of the square naturally clip the circular eye shape. Then I'm considering whether to add a small dark nostril bump near the bill base, using a nearest-surface-point lookup to position it correctly on the bill's ridge.

I'll skip serrated bill teeth since they'd likely add visual noise, but I do want a gold sector stripe on the upper bill combined with the orange-to-black band gradient already defined there.

Now I'm picking out the full color palette for the model—orange, gold, black, white, red, blue, leg gray, claw, and dark tones—and starting to sketch out the paint function for the body, figuring out how to define the white bib region using position and normal coordinates on the chest.

No perch needed since it's a standalone standing model. I'm checking off the key detail list: the eye ring, bill ridge and nostril, red undertail, clawed feet, white bib via paint, and scalloped wing extrusion. I'm weighing whether tiny feather cards on the head crest would add worthwhile detail or just over-engineer it.

Toucans don't have crests, so I'm dropping that idea, along with serrated bill teeth and a hidden tongue detail. Now I'm moving on to planning the rig: assigning joint roles like spine, head, jaw, wing, leg, tail, and digit, with the hips as the root spine joint, and figuring out which SDK exports I actually need to import for the module.

Writing import statement and meta object...

I'm defining the color palette for the toucan's plumage and features, then building a profile helper function to interpolate body radii at different heights along a key-based curve, and setting up the body shape keys that define the toucan's silhouette.

Now I'm working out the spine path using control points from rump to neck, planning a Catmull-Rom curve through them, and computing arc-length segments to map profile positions correctly along the curve.

Checking that the head sphere properly covers the top of the neck tube, with the neck joint aiming toward the correct target point so the chain stays consistent.

For the head joint, I'm attaching it to the neck joint with its own position and role, so the bill geometry rotates correctly with the head since it's defined in head-local coordinates. The jaw joint then parents off the head with a hinge rotation along the bone's local X axis so it can open and close naturally.

I'm deciding whether the rest pose should show a slightly open beak—maybe a small negative rotation on the jaw joint, since positive degrees tip a forward-pointing bone downward to open it. Since the jaw's bone inherits the head's up-forward orientation rather than pointing straight forward, I need to think through how that rotation axis actually affects the visible opening before settling on a value.

Posing the jaw after geometry is built should work fine since the joint transform carries the attached part with it. I'll go with a modest 6° rotation to crack the bill open slightly, trusting the stated convention that positive degrees tip a forward-pointing bone down—risky if the sign is wrong since it could make the bills intersect, but I'll trust the spec.

Now I'm working out the upper bill's curve so the tip sits about 0.2 units from its base, and checking that the base point tucks properly into the head sphere rather than floating outside it—adjusting the base z-coordinate slightly deeper so the bill root is buried convincingly into the face.

I'm defining the taper profile for the bill radius along its length, shrinking from a chunky base to a slimmer tip, and confirming the dorsal (top) side of the bill aligns with the bone's natural up-normal so the coloring sectors land correctly. Now I'm setting up the lower bill's jaw joint position and its bezier path, checking that the joint sits just slightly inside the head surface so the mouth hinge reads as anatomically grounded.

I'm figuring out the lower bill's radius taper and color bands, deciding orange fades to black near the tip to match the upper bill. Then I'm working out the eye decal placement relative to the bill base, computing distances from the head center to make sure the eye sits naturally beside the bill and slightly below the dorsal ridge, and considering whether the head needs any scale distortion versus staying a plain sphere.

I'm defining a shared plumage paint function using a dark mottled texture, then writing conditional paint rules for the body and head so the white throat/bib patch blends continuously from chest to neck based on normal direction and position thresholds. I also sketch out variants for the wing and tail surfaces, deciding to mostly reuse the same plumage with minor sector-based color overrides for the red undertail.

Now I'm building the spine chain from a sequence of body profile points, naming the joints hips/back/chest/neck, then sweeping a profile radius function along it with a moderate polygon side count for a slightly faceted, stylized look. I move on to the tail chain, attached to the hip joint, using a box-section sweep that tapers width while keeping a flat thin height, with a red sector carved into the underside tip for toucan coloring.

I'm setting up the leg chains for both sides using mirrored catmull-rom paths through hip, knee, ankle, and foot points, sweeping a simple tapering radius for a solid-colored leg, and extracting the foot tip joint to serve as the parent bone for individual toe segments. Now I'm working out toe placement and divergence angles coming off the foot, trying to approximate a zygodactyl toe arrangement with forward and backward offsets scaled by the side multiplier.

Now I'm rescaling the whole toucan down to realistic proportions, recomputing spine control points, profile radii, leg and tail joint positions, and bill curves so the overall height and length come out around 0.5-0.6m instead of my earlier oversized draft. I'm checking that the upper and lower bill overlap slightly at the base like a closed beak but gap open near the tip, and refining the eye placement so the decal sits right on the skull surface using a nearest-surface-point lookup that also supplies the correct outward-facing normal for the eye direction.

I'm sketching the nostril placement on the bill side using the same surface-nearest approach, then writing the SVG eye texture with concentric blue, gold, and black rings plus a white highlight dot. I'm working out toe positions and claw spike directions so the claws don't sink noticeably below the floor plane, and confirming joint roles and parent chains line up correctly for spine, tail, legs, wings, head, and jaw.

Writing component code...

I'm reasoning through how the body sweep's radius profile shapes the torso, how the leg capsule chain bends through hip-knee-ankle-foot, and how toe capsules and claw spikes attach as bones to the foot joint. For the wings, I'm drafting an extrude outline for the feather shape mirrored across both sides using the chest joint as parent, then placing the skull sphere and decal-based eyes using surface-nearest lookups on the head.
